body.p: Upon entry of the present amendment, claims 1-3, 6-8, 10, 11, 13, 17, 18, 20-22, 25-27, 29, 32, 41, and 54 will be pending in this application. Claims 1, 2, 3, 6, 8, 20, 21, 22, 25, 27, and 41 have been amended, and new claim 54 have been added. No new matter is added. Based on the following remarks, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of the pending claims.
Claims 2-3, 6, 8, 21-22, 25, 27, 32, and 41 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) as
allegedly being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention.

Specifically, the Office action alleges that "at least a portion" is a relative term which renders claims 2, 3, 6, 8, 21, 22, 25, 27, and 41 indefinite and "the change" in claim 32 has insufficient antecedent basis.

Claims 2, 3, 6, 8, 21, 22, 25, and 27 are amended by changing "at least a portion" to "at least one." Claim 41 is amended by deleting "at least a portion of" Claim 32 is amended by changing dependency to claim 20 and adding "further comprising a computer-readable medium storing instructions to generate an image based on a change in the one or more optical responses of the at least one optical sensor."
Claims 1-3, 7-8, 10-11, 20-22, 26-27, 29, and 41 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Pub. No. 2019/0083059 to Byrnes et al. ("Byrnes") in
view of U.S. Pub. No. 2013/0208562 to Shen ("Shen").
Claims 6 and 25 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over
Byrnes and Shen, and further in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2004/0039282 to Szabo et al. ("Szabo") and U.S. Pat. No. 5,410,516 to Uhlendorf et al. ("Uhlendorf').
Claims 13 and 32 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable
over Byrnes and Shen, and further in view of U. S. Pub. No. 2021/0349009 to Rozental et al. ("Rozental").
Claim 17 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Byrnes and Shen, and further in view of U.S. Pub. No. 2007/0237460 to Fan et al. ("Fan").
Claim 18 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as allegedly being unpatentable over Byrnes and Shen, and further in view U.S. Pub. No. 2010/0231903 to Sumetsky ("Sumetsky").
Independent claim 1 is amended to include "at least one optical sensor comprising

ultrasound enhancement material; ... the at least one optical sensor configured to produce one or more optical responses upon receiving harmonic and subharmonic ultrasound echoes, corresponding to the transmitted ultrasound signal, from the medium, the at least one optical sensor having a bandwidth greater than that of the at least one transducer."

Neither Byrne nor Shen teaches or makes obvious that the at least one optical sensor has a bandwidth greater than that of the at least one transducer, and the bandwidth of the at least one optical sensor ranges from at leastf/Mto Nf, Mand N being integers greater than 1, as specified in amended claim 1.

Byrne and Shen may include harmonic echoes, such as "second harmonic" (e.g., 2f) in Byrne or harmonic signals with frequencies of 2fo and 3fo, as cited in the Office action. Office action, p. 6. However, Neither Byrne nor Shen teaches or makes obvious subharmonic echoes, whose frequencies less than the fundamental frequencies, for examplefM, Mbeing an integer. Further, neither Byrne nor Shen teaches or makes obvious that an optical sensor has a bandwidth ranging from at least onef/Mto Nf, M and N being integers greater than 1. Such range extending tof/M allows the at least one optical sensor to sense and produce optical responses by receiving subharmonic ultrasound echoes.
In addition, neither Byrne nor Shen teaches or makes obvious that the at least one sensor comprises ultrasound enhancement material, as specified in amended claim 1.

Therefore, independent claim 1 is not obvious over Byrne and Shen. Independent claims 20 and 41 include substantially the same subject matter as claim 1. Thus, independent claims 20 and 41 are not obvious over Byrne and Shen. Claims 2, 3, 6, 8, 21, 22, 25, and 27 depend from one of the independent claims 1 or 12, so claims 2, 3, 6, 8, 21, 22, 25, and 27 are not obvious over the cited references at least based on the same reason for independent claim 1.

In view of the foregoing, Applicant believes all claims now pending in this application are in condition for allowance. The issuance of a formal Notice of Allowance at an early date is respectfully requested.
